title: SSE reassembly with function-call atomicity and backfill
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem:
Clients reconnecting to long-lived SSE streams sometimes receive fragments out-of-order or overlapping (partial token boundaries). This is particularly problematic when a fragment contains a tool/function call payload: double-executing a function on reconnect is unacceptable for many customers. Current implementations focus on resume cursors and simple sequence replay but lack a robust, cross-version-compatible reassembly and dedupe strategy for function calls and structured outputs.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic reassembly of split/overlapping fragments across reconnects without requiring strict per-chunk ACKs.
- Guarantee function-call atomicity semantics (at-most-once from application perspective) even with reconnects and partial fragments.
- Backfill missing fragments efficiently when clients supply a resume cursor + last-seen sequence.
- Maintain compatibility with older SDKs/clients (graceful negotiation).

Design proposal (summary):
1) Envelope changes (backwards-compatible): each SSE data chunk includes optional meta headers in the payload JSON: seq_id (monotonic per-connection), frag_index (0..n-1), frag_total (n), frag_checksum (sha1 hex for fragment payload), func_call_id (nullable, opaque id generated on first function call emission), event_type (token|function_call|complete|heartbeat), resume_cursor (server-sent position marker). These fields are optional; legacy clients ignore unknown fields.

2) Fragment window and reassembly heuristics:
- Server maintains a per-stream sliding reassembly window keyed by seq_id and resume_cursor. Window size default 256 fragments (configurable per-tenant).
- When reconnect occurs, client sends last_ack_seq and resume_cursor. Server computes missing seq ranges and emits a compact backfill sequence: events labeled event_type=backfill with frag_index/frag_total metadata to indicate contiguous reconstruction pieces.
- Overlapping/duplicate fragments are reconciled by comparing frag_checksum and fragment boundaries. If checksums match, server dedupes; if checksums differ but boundaries overlap, server uses boundary heuristics: prefer fragments containing valid JSON token boundaries (we run a lightweight token parser to detect likely JSON boundaries) and emit a reassembly_hint to client explaining conflicts for telemetry.

3) Function-call atomicity and dedupe layer:
- On first emission of a function call, server assigns func_call_id (UUIDv4) and includes it on every fragment that contains any portion of that call. The backend side (tools/router) must treat func_call_id as the idempotency key for invocation.
- If a reconnect/backfill would re-emit fragments with the same func_call_id, the tool layer will check a dedupe cache (TTL = 24h configurable) and skip duplicate invocations, returning the original result binding to the stream. This provides at-most-once semantics for function calls from user perspective while keeping stream semantics at-least-once for tokens.
- Dedupe cache is pluggable: Redis or in-process LRU for single-node Dedicated deployments. We will provide an abstraction in runtime that checks and stores (func_call_id, invocation_result_ref).

4) Resume and backfill protocol:
- Client reconnect request includes headers: X-RW-Resume-Cursor, X-RW-Last-Seq. Server responds with HTTP 200 and an initial backfill envelope describing the missing ranges as a compact array (only if there are gaps). Backfill events are emitted before new live events.
- To avoid large replays, server limits backfill volume per reconnect (default 100KB/10s) and will send a backfill_truncated marker with a canonical point for client to request a full history retrieval API if needed.

5) Compatibility layer and negotiation:
- Clients may include X-RW-Stream-Proto with supported minor version (e.g., 1 or 2). If not present, server emits minimal compat-only events and falls back to legacy framing (no frag_* fields).
- For older clients, we expose a shim where server performs reassembly server-side and presents a single reconstructed event rather than fragmented stream. This increases server CPU/memory but provides compatibility.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Memory vs correctness: larger reassembly windows reduce risk of losing fragments but increase memory and GC pressure on high-concurrency hosts. We'll default to conservative window sizes and expose tenant configs.
- Complexity vs latency: checksum and token-boundary parsing add CPU; parsing is async and batched to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Dedupe TTL: persistent dedupe storage provides stronger guarantees at cost of storage/operational complexity for Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosteds will use a distributed Redis cluster; Dedicated customers can optionally hook an external cache.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fragment checksum/dedupe logic, token-boundary heuristics, and backfill truncation behavior.
- Integration tests: reconnect scenarios with interleaved function calls, simulated packet loss, and artificial overlap cases.
- Interop tests: run against latest JS and Python SDKs for both modern and legacy negotiation modes.
- Canary: rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, measure duplicate_function_calls, reassembly_latency_p95, stream_reconnect_rate, backfill_truncated_rate.

Metrics & alerts:
- duplicate_function_calls (count, tags: tenant, region) -> Alert if > 0.1% of function calls in canary window.
- reassembly_latency_p50/95/99 -> monitor regression vs baseline.
- fragment_drop_rate, backfill_truncated_rate -> warn when > threshold.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement persistent, global exactly-once for non-function tokens. We accept at-least-once token emission and rely on semantic dedupe at application level for non-critical tokens.

Rollout & follow-ups:
- Phase 1: server-side runtime + tests + minimal SDK changes (JS/py) to pass resume headers and surface func_call_id as opaque to user.
- Phase 2: SDK helpers for automatic func_call_id generation and dedupe idempotency hooks.
- Phase 3: Admin console toggles for per-tenant window size and dedupe store choice.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/streaming/reassembly-fn-atomicity (internal)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4387
- Integration test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-testbed/tree/agg-reassembly

2026-02-16: Infra provided profiling: default window 256 fragments ~= 6MB per-stream metadata on peak; recommend 128 for shared hosts. - Colin (infra)
2026-02-22: Reviewed with PM (Jorge) and Design (Maya). PM asked for a customer-facing FAQ explaining duplicate avoidance semantics. Added to follow-ups. - Aisha
2026-02-27: Engineering review notes: Ravi requested that frag_checksum be optional to reduce overhead on low-latency paths; we'll make it enabled-by-config and required for backfill. - Ravi

2026-03-04: Added a small prototype in runtime that emits func_call_id and hooks into existing tool invocation path. Proof-of-concept against local Redis dedupe passing. PR opened: runtime#4387. - Ravi

2026-03-09: QA reported a flaky case where overlapping fragments with differing checksums produced incorrect merge; introduced stronger token-boundary detection and a conflict telemetry event. Re-running tests. - QA team
2026-03-12: Preparing canary rollout plan: 10% traffic in us-west-2, monitor duplicate_function_calls (alert if > 0.05%). Production rollout contingent on canary metrics. - Aisha
